title: API Runtime
html:
Setup · API principles · OpenAPI · Validation

The Fastify API runtime provides configuration, structured logging and tracing, health/lifecycle behavior, the public error envelope, optional PostgreSQL access through Prisma, and optional bearer access-token verification. Product capabilities are modules composed in src/modules.ts. The web application consumes the generated API contract through the workspace SDK package (packages/sdk). The composed identity module implements Keycloak login and server-managed human sessions without handling passwords; see identity and sessions.

Find the owning implementation

Concern Source
Configuration and process composition src/config.ts, src/main.ts
HTTP boundary, lifecycle, and failures src/app.ts, src/lifecycle.ts, src/errors.ts
Module contract and composition src/module.ts, src/modules.ts, src/error-registry.ts
Database client and token verification src/database.ts, src/authentication.ts
Prisma schema, schema meaning, and runtime grants prisma/schema/, prisma/metadata/, prisma/runtime-grants/, reviewed prisma/migrations/
Generated references generate-references.ts, openapi.ts, database-reference.ts
Process smokes scripts/smoke.mjs and module smokes in scripts/smoke/

Modules

A module is one cohesive API capability. It implements the ApiModule contract in src/module.ts: a name, an OpenAPI tag, its requirements (database, authentication), its executable operations, its public error codes, and an activate function that mounts routes once its requirements are configured. Shared runtime files never import a module; src/modules.ts is the only composition point, and dependency rules enforce that boundary.

Keep a module's files together under its name: src/features/<module>/ for domain, application, persistence, contracts, routes, and errors; prisma/schema/<module>.prisma for its models; prisma/metadata/<module>.json for table meaning; prisma/runtime-grants/<module>.sql for least-privilege runtime access; a reviewed migration; tests under test/<module>/; and an optional emitted-process smoke at scripts/smoke/<module>.ts. Follow application boundaries, dependency rules, and the database policies. Orion's reference implementation is a complete example.

Outside production, a module whose requirements are not configured stays unmounted. In production, startup fails instead, so a composed capability cannot silently disappear. Generated OpenAPI and the public error registry always include every composed module, whether or not it is configured locally.

Local commands

Use setup for the frozen install, generated Prisma client, environment loading, containers, and startup order. pnpm -C apps/api dev loads the ignored root .env.local when present; start runs emitted code and expects its process environment without loading that file.

From the repository root:

Purpose Command
Generate ignored Prisma client pnpm -C apps/api db:generate
Apply committed migrations to the configured database pnpm -C apps/api db:migrate:deploy
Check API behavior/types pnpm -C apps/api test and pnpm -C apps/api typecheck
Emit/start API pnpm -C apps/api build, then pnpm -C apps/api start
Intentionally regenerate tracked API/database/configuration/error references pnpm -C apps/api references:write
Check current API/database/SDK references without editing them pnpm references:check

Tests and reference generation use fresh migrated Testcontainers PostgreSQL, and identity tests also start the pinned Keycloak image, so a compatible container runtime must be reachable. Follow the artifact workflow for downstream SDK/portal generation after source changes. The root pnpm validate also checks emitted builds, real-process recovery, and browser behavior; a focused package check alone does not replace it.

Configuration and database access

config.ts is the sole runtime environment parser; the generated configuration reference owns the setting catalog. ORION_ENV is always required. ORION_DATABASE_URL enables the database for modules that require it and adds a bounded database check to readiness. ORION_TOKEN_ISSUER, ORION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE, and ORION_TOKEN_JWKS_URL enable bearer authentication and must be configured together.

ORION_DATABASE_URL is the restricted runtime credential. Only the Prisma CLI reads ORION_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL, supplied separately for migration commands; the CLI does not automatically load the API's root .env.local. Keep both out of tracked files and do not leave the migration credential in the runtime environment.

The runtime role needs USAGE on the application schema plus only the table and column privileges that each module declares in prisma/runtime-grants/. It needs no DDL grant. The database fixture provisions separate migration/runtime roles and applies those grants, so integration tests run with the same least-privilege runtime role.

The release workflow owns durable migration recording. An empty registry is not permission to rewrite unverified history.

Identity and sessions

The identity module owns application principals and PostgreSQL-backed browser sessions under the identity and session design. It requires the database, the token settings and the six TELUNI_ human identity settings, and stays unmounted outside production until they are configured. Login, callback and back-channel logout are public browser/provider routes under /auth; session routes and every product module that needs a human authenticate through its session boundary, exposed to other modules only by src/features/identity/public.ts. That boundary passes the stored provider access token through the unchanged verifier below, so the cookie never bypasses it. Bearer-only requests without a session are rejected by session-protected operations.

The realm contract is provisioned by scripts/identity-realm.ts and qualified against the pinned Keycloak image in scripts/keycloak.ts. Identity tests start that image and PostgreSQL through Testcontainers.

Organizations

The organizations module depends on the identity session boundary. It owns companies, branches, creator memberships, responsibility, standard-role grants and branch scopes, and append-only organization audit under D-01. Every request resolves current tenant access; administrator and manager grants require strong authentication. Company creation is idempotent per principal/key and atomically creates the creator relationships and audit event. Company and branch changes use expected versions and write audit in the same transaction. Branch and audit pagination reject invalid or incorrectly bound cursors. Runtime grants exclude tenant-column changes, audit edits/deletion and membership/grant administration that has no implemented operation.

The mail module owns the transactional outbound-email outbox under ADR-0026. It requires the database and the TELUNI_MAIL_ settings (which also need TELUNI_PUBLIC_ORIGIN) and stays unmounted outside production until they are configured. Producers enqueue messages inside their own transactions through src/features/mail/public.ts; the dispatcher starts when the server is ready, claims due messages with expiring leases, submits them through SMTP at least once with bounded retries, and stops during shutdown drain.

The invitations module, composed from the organizations feature, requires organizations and mail and owns company invitations under D-13: administrators and branch managers invite by email, and the person signed in with the invited verified address accepts with the credential from the email link in a request body. Organizations keeps working without it when mail is not configured.

The two-company suite runs against migrated PostgreSQL as the restricted runtime role; its synthetic session port is confined to the test. The organizations browser journeys use the real identity stack. Platform/support access and bulk operations remain pending in PJ-03/PJ-24.

Devices

The devices module requires identity, organizations, the database and TELUNI_DEVICE_CODE_KEYS, and owns screen enrollment, pairing and lifecycle under ADR-0027 and the device enrollment design. A player starts an anonymous enrollment with the hash of a credential it generated, shows the returned code, and polls until a person with devices.manage on the target branch claims the code in the panel. Device routes authenticate that credential as a bearer token; check-in renews offline authorization for seven days. Unlinking is irreversible and leaves erasure pending until the device confirms it or a person records a controlled reset. Archiving a branch with active screens is refused with BRANCH_IN_USE. A screen may carry an explicit IANA time zone; otherwise it follows its branch, and GET /device/self returns the effective zone. The two-company suite covers claims, limits, concurrency, scope, rotation and erasure against migrated PostgreSQL.

Media

The media module requires identity, organizations, the database and TELUNI_MEDIA_STORAGE_PATH, and owns the company media library under ADR-0028 and the media library design. A person with media.upload creates an item for the company or one branch, then streams its bytes with PUT .../content (application/octet-stream, exact declared length); uploads alone may run longer than the standard 30-second request limit. An in-process processor inspects and converts each upload with FFmpeg into a display rendition and a thumbnail, and the item becomes READY or REJECTED with a reason. Content is served with range support, nosniff and a sandboxing CSP. Archive, delete (to a 30-day trash), restore and discard use expected versions; registered reference guards block deleting media in use. FFmpeg/ffprobe 6.1 or later are required; production refuses to start without them. The two-company suite processes synthetic media with real FFmpeg against migrated PostgreSQL.

Programming

The programming module requires identity, organizations, devices, media and the database, and owns playlists, programming groups, the draft programs of groups and screens with their schedule rules, screen assignments and timelines under the programming design and ADR-0029. Playlists belong to the company or one branch and replace their ordered items as a whole; groups span the whole company or fixed branches; each output's rules are saved as a complete set after wall-clock conflict validation, and a rule check returns conflicting pairs before saving. Timelines evaluate a screen's source in its own time zone (explicit, otherwise its branch's) or a group's program in a chosen zone with the pure evaluator in schedule.ts, whose canonical fixtures the player will share. An assignment needs explicit confirmation only while its destination has no publication, which the publications module answers through the programming port. Playlists protect their media from deletion, explicit group spans protect branches from archiving, and a screen moved outside its group's span leaves the group in the move's transaction. The two-company suite runs against migrated PostgreSQL with the real organizations, devices and media modules.

The publications module requires identity, organizations, devices, media, programming, the database and TELUNI_SYNC_SIGNING_KEYS, and owns publications, the screen synchronization exchange and screens' synchronization reports under the publication and synchronization design and ADR-0030. A check builds a program's draft into its publication content and lists what blocks it; publishing needs the content digest the person reviewed and stores the generation's exact manifest bytes, while equal content returns the latest publication. Screens poll POST /device/sync with their device credential, receive the desired publication computed from current rows and an ES256 authorization statement, and download only that publication's manifest and display renditions; reports become each screen's state and 30-day transitions for the panel. Retained publications protect their media from deletion and hourly maintenance prunes those past 90 days. The two-company suite runs against migrated PostgreSQL with the real organizations, devices, media and programming modules and simulated screens.

Identity and contract

The shared token verifier accepts verified at+jwt tokens signed with RS256 or ES256 by the configured issuer for the configured audience. It validates expiration and requires nonempty sub, valid issuance/expiry timing, a stable orion_principal_id UUID, orion_actor_type=human, and a string scope. It yields the principal ID and the issuer-granted scopes; product modules also enforce current session and application-owned memberships. Stored ownership must survive provider changes; request bodies cannot grant identity or capability. The authentication policy and ADR-0012 govern this boundary. Keycloak is selected and locally qualified; no real environment is provisioned.

Executable module contracts own operations, stable operation IDs, typed inputs/outputs, and expected failures. The OpenAPI reference includes health and every composed module's operations; the error reference derives from the shared and module registries.

Request protection

A module that exposes authenticated routes should apply request limiting before token verification and database access, as the reference module does with a process-local source-IP limit; health probes stay outside it. Exhaustion returns 429 RATE_LIMITED in the public envelope with a bounded Retry-After. This is resource protection, not a product quota.

Screen (device credential) routes are the exception to source-IP keying, because many screens share one address behind a store's router or the ingress proxy: registerDeviceRequestLimits counts each presented credential (a digest, never the credential) on its own under a ceiling of 6,000 requests per address per minute.

Process-local limiting uses the direct peer address; trusted proxies are not configured. A multi-replica or reverse-proxy deployment must define shared/edge limiting and trusted client-IP handling before promising fleet-wide or per-user limits.

Lifecycle and diagnostics

main.ts validates configuration, initializes Pino/OpenTelemetry, then dynamically imports Fastify, Prisma, and composed modules before listening. Preserve that order for instrumented infrastructure. Incoming W3C trace context propagates; each request receives a fresh server-generated x-request-id. Errors follow the public envelope. Logs and traces identify the service by the API package name.

Startup reports initialization, liveness reports process-local health, and readiness becomes unavailable while draining or when a configured database is unavailable. A configured database is probed before readiness and through a bounded readiness check. SIGINT/SIGTERM trigger bounded HTTP, database, and telemetry shutdown.

Logs and exported spans/metric dimensions use allowlisted operational fields. The runtime does not log payloads, raw URLs, headers, configuration objects, or arbitrary exception messages. Unexpected failures produce one sanitized diagnostic occurrence. A readiness failure or a lost response cannot prove that a prior write failed; see delivery and side effects.
